claims.statement: Milo Shen-Orr Itzkovitz Kashtan Chklovskii Alon six-author Network Motifs paper appeared Science 298(5594) pp824-827 Oct25 2002
claims.locator: Original Science issue pdf and PubMed publisher

claims.statement: Network motifs are patterns statistically overrepresented compared to suitably randomized networks, not just common subgraphs
2002 survey counted 3 and 4 vertex directed subgraphs in transcriptional biological ecological neuro and technological networks
Randomized graphs preserve each vertex in/out degree and account for occurrence numbers of n-1 subgraphs to strengthen null comparison
2002 paper defines motif selection by randomization tail probability P < .01 under its chosen testing procedure
E coli and S cerevisiae regulatory networks exhibited feed-forward loop 3-vertex motif and bi-fan 4-vertex motif overrepresentation
Among seven studied food webs certain motifs shared and feed-forward loop underrepresented relative random controls
Study compared C elegans neural network and electronics WWW as additional systems and identified network-type motif patterns
On three labeled vertices with six possible directed edges, 2^6=64 edge sets; non-isomorphic connected directed triads number 13
Feedforward loop edges A→B, B→C, A→C are an acyclic oriented transitive triangle, unlike directed feedback cycle
claims.locator: Science Fig1 motif naming; graph-theoretic proof

claims.statement: Directed six-node graph edges AB AC BC DE DF EF CD contains exactly two FFLs; swapping endpoints AB and DE to AE and DB preserves each node in/out degrees yet leaves zero FFL
claims.locator: author-defined directed edge swap independently enumerated with graph code

claims.statement: Z=(N_real-mean_null)/sd_null is explanatory normalized deviation, not original paper's unique formal motif acceptance criterion
claims.locator: distinguished from original empirical tail probability

claims.statement: Detected overrepresented subgraph does not independently establish necessary biological function, evolutionary selection or unique mechanism
claims.locator: original article methodological limitations and qualified inference

claims.statement: Historical SIR-style 1927 Kermack McKendrick epidemic model predates modern network motif work; next volume deliberately returns to theoretical prehistory
claims.locator: Royal Society original bibliographic record; chapter outline
